abuseArticles.title: Financial abuse
abuseArticles.summary: A person may control access to money, work, housing, benefits, or create debt in someone else’s name to limit their choices.
abuseArticles.sign: You may be prevented from seeing accounts, required to account for every purchase, or pressured to hand over income.
abuseArticles.support: If safe, consider talking with a specialist advocate from a device the other person cannot access.

abuseArticles.title: Physical abuse
abuseArticles.summary: Physical abuse includes intentional force or threats of force that cause injury, pain, fear, or restrict movement.
abuseArticles.sign: It can include hitting, pushing, restraint, blocking someone from leaving, or damaging belongings to intimidate.
abuseArticles.support: If you are in immediate danger, call 112 when it is safe to do so. You deserve care without blame.

abuseArticles.title: Sexual abuse
abuseArticles.summary: Sexual contact or activity without freely given consent is abuse. Consent can be withdrawn at any time and is not implied by a relationship.
abuseArticles.sign: Pressure, threats, unwanted touching, or taking advantage when someone cannot consent are not consent.
abuseArticles.support: You can seek medical or emotional support whether or not you choose to report what happened.

abuseArticles.title: Emotional and psychological abuse
abuseArticles.summary: Repeated humiliation, intimidation, threats, isolation, or blame can be used to undermine someone’s confidence and autonomy.
abuseArticles.sign: You might feel afraid to disagree, cut off from people you trust, or constantly responsible for another person’s reactions.
abuseArticles.support: A trusted person or domestic-violence advocate can help you think through options at your pace.

abuseArticles.title: Digital abuse and stalking
abuseArticles.summary: Technology can be used to monitor, threaten, impersonate, or repeatedly contact someone without their consent.
abuseArticles.sign: Examples include account access without permission, location tracking, repeated unwanted messages, or sharing private images.
abuseArticles.support: Use a safer device if possible before changing accounts or settings. Sudden changes can sometimes be noticed.

abuseArticles.title: Coercive control
abuseArticles.summary: A repeated pattern of controlling behaviour can take away freedom, even when there is no physical assault.
abuseArticles.sign: This can involve isolation, monitoring, threats, control of money, or dictating everyday choices.
abuseArticles.support: You do not need to decide on a label before asking for support or making a safety plan.
